title: Hypercore POC scoping - workload modeling
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for Hypercore's in-product summarization pipeline. Discussed QPS/concurrency targets, input/output token distributions, latency SLOs, benchmark plan, and timelines for a 6-week POC. Action items: Redwood to run baseline benchmark with sample traces, share POC plan and pricing, customer to provide anonymized request trace and success criteria.
next_steps: Rachel to send POC plan and pricing sheet by 2026-04-02
Hypercore to share 7-day anonymized request trace and sample prompt set by 2026-04-05
Redwood SE to schedule baseline benchmark run w/ Hypercore tokens week of 2026-04-06
Follow-up meeting to review benchmark results and finalize capacity sizing on 2026-04-15
action_items: Rachel: send POC plan, pricing, and SOW template - due 2026-04-02
Priya: export and anonymize 7 days of traffic (incl headers, prompt length distribution) - due 2026-04-05
Dmitri: run baseline perf benchmark using sample traces and report QPS/concurrency curves - due 2026-04-10
Daniel: confirm VPC connectivity requirements for private POC - due 2026-04-08
transcript:
[00:00] Rachel (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna focus on the workload side for the POC, specifically the qps and concurrency you expect and token distributions. um quick quick intros.
[00:12] Liam (Hypercore): hey liam here, cto. priya and daniel on the call too. thanks rachel.
[00:18] Priya (Hypercore): priya - head of ml. main use case is in-product summarization for customer support tickets, mixed short/long inputs.
[00:25] Rachel (Redwood): perfect. dmitri is our se, he'll walk through measurement approach and benchmark plan. dmitri over to you.
[00:33] Dmitri (Redwood SE): thanks rachel. so from experience we scope these by three signals: steady qps, burst concurrency, and the input/output token length distribution. i'll throw out some templates and we can align.
[00:45] Dmitri (Redwood SE): can you give ballpark qps? like average requests per second and peak?
[00:50] Priya (Hypercore): avg is around 8 qps right now, peaks to maybe 120 for short bursts during business hours, and concurrency per model instance is usually 60 ish when the mobile agents hit.
[01:02] Rachel (Redwood): ok so avg 8 qps, peak 120 qps, concurrency observed 60. what's the tail latency tolerance?
[01:10] Liam (Hypercore): we want 95th < 300ms ideally for the summary generation, 99th < 700ms is acceptable. cost is also a factor, we have a target tco per 1M tokens.
[01:21] Dmitri (Redwood SE): good. for modeling we'll need the input token distribution - like percentiles for input length and output length. even a histogram helps.
[01:30] Priya (Hypercore): most inputs are short 1-50 tokens 55% of traffic, 25% are medium 50-250 tokens, and 20% are long 250-2k tokens. outputs average 40-120 tokens depending on summarization depth.
[01:45] Dmitri (Redwood SE): that's helpful. so traffic is bimodal-ish. for initial bench we'll model the mix: 55% short, 25% medium, 20% long. also want to know prompt templates — are you including attachments or structured context?
[01:58] Priya (Hypercore): we strip attachments, but we do include conversation history up to 2k tokens sometimes for context; it's not every request.
[02:06] Rachel (Redwood): ok noted. another question: are you looking at hosted api or dedicated / private?
[02:11] Liam (Hypercore): security is important — we prefer Dedicated in our cloud account, maybe Private later. for POC we can do dedicated reserved capacity. we need ksm and audit logs too.
[02:23] Dmitri (Redwood SE): understood. Dedicated works well for baseline perf. we'll propose a config — e.g., 2x A100-style nodes for the initial run with quantized 4-bit model variant and batch tuning.
[02:35] Daniel (Hypercore): what about kv cache and batching? our traffic has a lot of repeated prefixes, can we cache?
[02:41] Dmitri (Redwood SE): yes we support prefix / KV caching. that'll reduce cost for repeated sessions. for sizing we model hit rate; can you estimate cache hit percent?
[02:50] Priya (Hypercore): maybe 30% prefix hit on weekdays.
[02:54] Dmitri (Redwood SE): ok put 30% cache hit into the model. that lowers tokens served by roughly that percent for cached prefixes.
[03:02] Rachel (Redwood): on success criteria, what are the must-haves vs nice-to-haves?
[03:07] Liam (Hypercore): must-haves: 95th latency below 300ms for short requests, output quality parity with our baseline model (we'll share eval prompts), and predictable cost estimates. nice-to-have: auto-scaling integration and canary rollouts.
[03:20] Priya (Hypercore): also need SOC2-level audit logs during the POC and SSO for dashboard access.
[03:26] Alex (Redwood): we can provide audit logs and SSO via SAML; we'll include the security pack in the POC doc.
[03:33] Dmitri (Redwood SE): benchmark plan: we'll run three phases — baseline single-node perf for each token bucket, multi-concurrency stress test to map QPS->p95/p99 latency, and production-like mixed traffic with synthetic traces derived from your anonymized logs.
[03:49] Dmitri (Redwood SE): metrics we'll collect: tokens per second, effective qps, per-request latency percentiles, GPU utilization, batch sizes, cost per 1M tokens estimate.
[03:58] Rachel (Redwood): timeline? we propose kickoff next week, trace handoff by 2026-04-05, baseline bench 2026-04-06 to 04-09, mixed-traffic runs 04-10 to 04-13, results review 04-15. does that work?
[04:12] Liam (Hypercore): sounds reasonable. need to sync with infra for VPC peering window.
[04:17] Daniel (Hypercore): we can open a maintenance window 04-07 for initial peering, daniel will confirm.
[04:23] Priya (Hypercore): on benchmarks, how do you model cost? do you include caching and batching gains?
[04:29] Dmitri (Redwood SE): yes our tooling will simulate caching hit rates, batching behavior based on inter-arrival times, and quantization profiles. we'll give a per-1M-token cost estimate for both hosted and dedicated.
[04:40] Rachel (Redwood): one common gotcha is tail-latency spikes on long inputs; we'll simulate tail-heavy traffic and show p99 deltas.
[04:47] Priya (Hypercore): we also need to see throughput at concurrency 60 since mobile bursts will lead to that.
[04:54] Dmitri (Redwood SE): noted. we'll run a concurrency sweep up to 200 concurrent requests so you can see headroom.
[04:59] Rachel (Redwood): any data residency requirements?
[05:02] Liam (Hypercore): Europe-only for EU customers; POC data can be on east US but production needs eu-west.
[05:09] Alex (Redwood): we'll note regions; dedicated nodes can be in eu-west for later.
[05:14] Rachel (Redwood): ok recap — we need: 1) anonymized 7-day trace with token lengths, timestamps, and a sample prompt set; 2) Redwood runs baseline and mixed benchmarks; 3) Redwood sends POC plan + pricing; 4) follow-up 2026-04-15 to review.
[05:30] Priya (Hypercore): quick question — how do you handle function/tool calling and structured outputs for summarization?
[05:36] Dmitri (Redwood SE): we support structured output and post-processing hooks; we'll include examples of function calling. keeps quality stable.
[05:44] Liam (Hypercore): any blockers on our side?
[05:46] Rachel (Redwood): we need trace export and a point of contact for infra. the rest we can provision.
[05:51] Daniel (Hypercore): i'll be infra contact. i'll share peering details and network policy.
[05:56] Rachel (Redwood): great. we'll follow up with a doc and dates. thanks everyone.
[05:59] Priya (Hypercore): thanks, bye.
[06:02] Rachel (Redwood): bye.
notes: Customer: Hypercore Systems, use case: in-product summarization for support tickets
Traffic mix: 55% short 1-50 tokens, 25% medium 50-250, 20% long 250-2k
Avg QPS: 8, peak QPS: 120, concurrency observed 60
Success criteria: p95 < 300ms for short requests, quality parity with baseline model, predictable cost estimates
POC timeline: kickoff asap, traces by 2026-04-05, benchmarks 2026-04-06 to 04-13, results review 2026-04-15
